newsitem.title: USA: Westcoast confirms McMahon plant gas cuts.
newsitem.headline: Westcoast confirms McMahon plant gas cuts.

text.p: Westcoast Energy confirmed Thursday that gas production at its McMahon gas processing plant in northeastern British Columbia had been cut by about one-fourth.
"We're at about 76 to 77 percent of contract demand. It will probably stay that way through the weekend," said company spokeswoman Patricia Bowles.
"We're still working on the problems...It's got to do with the sulfur plant," she added.
Bowles said the plant's capacity is rated at 650 million cubic feet of gas a day (mmcfd), indicating that the current cuts would be around 160 mmcfd.
McMahon, which is a central collection point for gas pipelines in western Canada.

Traders earlier Thursday said news of more problems at the 30-year-old plant sent spot prices 10 cents higher into the US$1.20-1.25 per mmBtu range at Sumas, Wash., the main export point for Canadian gas into the U.S. west coast market said.
On Wednesday, the company said it had declared a force majeure due to constraints at its sulfur plant. The force majeure was lifted shortly thereafter.
The plant was also shut for a few hours on Tuesday after mechanical problems occurred in its control system.
